stem.text: Let f be the function defined by \( f(x) = \begin{cases} \frac{x^{2} + 8 x + 12}{x + 2}, & x \ne -2 \\ -4, & x = -2 \end{cases} \). Determine whether f is continuous at \( x = -2 \), and justify your answer.

answer_key.label: f is not continuous at \( x = -2 \), because the limit of f(x) there is 4 while f(-2) = -4.

worked_solution.text: The function value at the boundary is \( f(-2) = -4 \), from the second line of the rule.
worked_solution.rule_named: evaluate the function at the input

worked_solution.text: For \( x \ne -2 \) the quotient simplifies to \( x + 6 \), so \( \lim_{x \to -2} f(x) = 4 \) from both sides.
The limit exists and equals 4, but \( f(-2) = -4 \), so the limit does not equal the function value and f is not continuous at \( x = -2 \).
worked_solution.rule_named: the limit must equal the function value

options.derivation: x = -2 substituted into the quotient, which applies only for x not equal to -2, giving 0/0
